title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing from the previous pages). X is a smooth (orbi)space, here a moduli space M_{g,ν} or its compactification. Θ is a normal-crossings divisor at infinity. It gives a filtration X=Θ^(0) ⊃ Θ^(1)=Θ ⊃ Θ^(2) ⊃ …. D' is a (normalised) stratum of codimension d and D'^* its open part. N_{D',Y} is the normal bundle and V_{D',Y} a tubular neighbourhood. V^*_{D',Y} is the deleted tubular neighbourhood (the complement of the divisor inside V). P_{D'^*} is the corresponding 'punctured normal' space: the normal bundle minus its coordinate hyperplanes, or its torus/sphere-bundle retract, over D'^*.

On the previous page Grothendieck constructed a morphism V^*_{D',Y} → P_{D'^*} (241), giving π1 V^* → π1 P (242). He also noted the difficulty that connectedness is not available without restrictive generic hypotheses.

On this page he changes strategy, following an earlier text of his own ('Mon p. 779 ff'; identity of that text unsure). Instead of a map V^* → P he defines an arrow in the opposite direction:
(243) Π_1^{ouv} P_{D'^*} → Π̃_1 V^*_{D',Y}.
- The source is the fundamental groupoid in the naive sense: objects are points, morphisms are homotopy classes of paths.
- The target 'necessarily' (on n'a pas le choix!) is a fundamental groupoid defined via simply connected (universal) coverings, i.e. via fibre functors.

The point is that a point of P (a normal direction at a point of the stratum) is not a point of V^*. It still determines a germ of sector in V^*, hence a fibre functor on coverings of V^*. That is exactly the mechanism of tangential base points: P-points act as base points 'at infinity' for V^*. Hence the Covering-theoretic definition is forced on the target.

He declines to give details. He also wonders whether this 'ménage' is needed at all, or whether one could work directly with Π_1 V^*_{D,Y} instead of Π_1 P_{D^*}, modifying the definition of the groupoids Π̃_{d_0,d_1,…,d_r}. These groupoids are attached to flags of strata of codimensions d_0<…<d_r, the building blocks of the 'structure at infinity'.

The page ends with a requirement for later: the natural map Π̃_{d_0…d_r} → Π_{d_0…d_r} must be an extension of groupoids whose kernel is a quotient of T_{d_0…d_r}. This T is the abelian group (lattice) generated by the loops around the local branches of Θ, i.e. the π1 of the torus fibres of the punctured normal bundle. For moduli of curves this is the group generated by commuting Dehn twists along the vanishing cycles.

In modern language, the page sets up a model of the boundary homotopy type of a normal-crossings compactification. It consists of a diagram, indexed by flags of strata, of fundamental groupoids of strata and of their deleted tubular neighbourhoods (homotopy links). Each link groupoid is a central-ish extension of the stratum groupoid by a quotient of Z^d. Base points are taken tangentially.
errors: No mathematical error is visible; the page is programmatic.

The kernel claim ('quotient of T') is correctly hedged. In the orbifold/stack setting of M_{g,ν}, automorphisms and branches of Θ that are not unibranch along the stratum can make the map from Z^d non-injective, or make the extension non-central (monodromy can permute branches). Grothendieck's 'quotient' and 'etc.' acknowledge this, but the precise conditions are left open.
Gap: the generalisation of 'loc. cit.' needed to define (243) without generic connectedness hypotheses is explicitly not carried out.

ideas.what: Define the comparison arrow from the groupoid of the punctured normal bundle P_{D^*} to the groupoid of the deleted tubular neighbourhood V^*. Points of P serve as base points (fibre functors) for coverings of V^*, so the target must be defined via universal coverings.
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points / fundamental groupoid with base points at infinity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points'); used by Ihara–Nakamura and others for M_{g,n}
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to base points and the Teichmüller tower near infinity; La Longue Marche (1981) contains related constructions, unsure of details

ideas.what: Groupoids Π̃_{d_0,…,d_r} indexed by flags of strata, with Π̃ → Π an extension whose kernel is a quotient of the local-monodromy lattice T_{d_0…d_r}.
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy links / exit-path (stratified) fundamental groupoid of a normal-crossings stratification; for M_{g,n}, the free abelian subgroups generated by Dehn twists along a multicurve (stabilisers of simplices of the curve complex)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (homotopy links, 1988), MacPherson / Treumann / Lurie (exit paths); Harvey, Ivanov, Boggi, Nakamura for the boundary of M_{g,n}
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (§'Lego', dévissage of stratified structures) in spirit only

ideas.what: Using the naive points-and-paths Π1 for the source and the covering-theoretic Π1 for the target.
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of the path groupoid with the Galois groupoid (fibre functors)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly reverses the comparison map so that points of the punctured normal bundle act as fibre functors on coverings of the deleted tubular neighbourhood. This is the tangential-base-point mechanism, set up here for every stratum of a normal-crossings boundary, and organised over flags of strata.
missed.quote: je vais plutôt … définir une flèche en sens inverse (243) Π_1^{ouv} P_{D^*} → Π̃_1 V^*_{D',Y} … le deuxième (on n'a pas le choix!) est défini en termes de rev. 1-connexes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a further documented instance of Grothendieck independently framing tangential/boundary base points as fibre functors, systematically along a stratification. It is of mainly historical interest, since the idea is now standard (Deligne, Ihara–Nakamura, Boggi's work on boundary groupoids).

missed.claim: Open question left by Grothendieck: can the whole flag-indexed groupoid structure at infinity be built directly from the Π_1 of deleted tubular neighbourhoods instead of the punctured normal bundles? He also leaves open the precise kernel of Π̃_{d_0…d_r} → Π_{d_0…d_r} (a quotient of T).
missed.quote: s'il n'est pas loisible de travailler … directement avec les Π_1 V^*_{D,Y} au lieu des Π_1 P_{D^*} … extension …, de noyau un quotient du T_{d_0,…,d_r}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is essentially answered in modern stratified homotopy theory, where homotopy links and exit paths make the two approaches equivalent. So the thread is largely resolved, not missed.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a working note that redirects the construction (reversing an arrow, choosing a covering-theoretic Π1) without new results. The underlying ideas (tangential base points, abelian local-monodromy kernels at boundary strata) are by now standard and partly anticipated in Grothendieck's circulated texts.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'non hyp. singulières' is doubtful. The image reads more like '[sans/nos] hyp. génériques', consistent with the previous page's 'hypothèses génériques'.
(243): the subscript on P should be D'^* (with prime), i.e. Π_1^{ouv} P_{D'^*} → Π̃_1 V^*_{D',Y}, with a tilde over the second Π_1.
'ce ménage est indispensable': the word before 'ménage' is overwritten/inserted; 'ménage' fits the image.

Last lines: the reading is likely 'que Π̃_{d_0…d_r} → Π_{d_0…d_r} soit une extension …, de noyau un quotient du T_{d_0,…,d_r} etc.'. 'extension d'extension' is doubtful; the first word may be 'structure'.
Line 2: the reference 'Mon p. 779 ff' is uncertain; it may be an abbreviation of one of Grothendieck's own manuscripts (possibly La Longue Marche).
